transcript_header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (NexaHealth - Head of ML), Diego Ramos (NexaHealth - Infra), Priya Nair (NexaHealth - Security)
Recording: yes
Notes: weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding, access, environment readiness, and next benchmark steps
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining we can start. hope you all had a good week. uh quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Thompson: hi yes maya here.
[00:10] Diego Ramos: diego on infra.
[00:12] Priya Nair: priya here.
[00:14] Samir Patel: samir from redwood se, thanks.
[00:17] Avery Chen: cool, agenda is quick onboarding status, access + network, then benchmark/runbook and next steps.
[00:26] Maya Thompson: sounds good. We did some work on the sample data export, but haven't handed keys over yet.
[00:32] Diego Ramos: yeah we blocked on the service account; security wants to review the KMS usage and peering details.
[00:38] Priya Nair: correct, we need to confirm where logs live, retention, and whether redwood will touch any PHI.
[00:45] Avery Chen: understood we'll share the security binder and SOC2 summary in the next 48 hours. that should answer logs, retention, and data flows. also note our dedicated offering keeps the control plane separate for private deployments.
[00:58] Samir Patel: quick technical note: for the benchmark we typically run a 100k message pass with a mix of short and long contexts to reproduce latency and cost numbers. we'll want remote access to the S3 bucket and a service account with read-only perms to the dataset.
[01:12] Diego Ramos: ok that works. On the VPC side we plan to peer with dedicated subnets, but need the redwood ip ranges and the expected ports.
[01:22] Avery Chen: I'll send the network diagram and concrete IP ranges; ports are standard TLS 443 plus the control plane egress to our telemetry endpoints. we can also support private peering for dedicated customers.
[01:34] Priya Nair: about KMS we use AWS KMS with strict key rotation, HSM-backed. do you support customer-managed keys?
[01:42] Samir Patel: yes, we support CMEK/KMS for private installs and Dedicated via our KMS integration. for hosted pilots we can also set up an envelope encryption pattern so you keep the root key. note: some small differences in the setup path between hosted vs dedicated.
[01:57] Maya Thompson: great. One of our concerns is latency vs cost. we need tail latency below 350ms for short prompts, and our budget target is about $0.0008 per token equivalent. is that realistic?
[02:12] Samir Patel: for short prompts if you stay on a medium-sized instance pool with batching disabled for low-latency prep, you can get 200-300ms p95 on optimized models. cost depends a lot on the model quantization and batching. we can show a few profiles in the benchmark.
[02:28] Diego Ramos: what about KV cache / prefix caching? we have conversational sessions and want to avoid re-sending long context every time.
[02:36] Samir Patel: we've got prefix caching and session-aware KV cache in the runtime. but for initial pilot we'll test without cache to measure baseline, then enable caching to demonstrate cost savings. there was a small typo in our last doc calling it 'KV cash' but it's 'KV cache' sorry.
[02:52] Maya Thompson: ha, yep saw that. also, can you confirm data residency? our legal requires EU-only for EU patients.
[02:59] Avery Chen: yes, we can pin region. Dedicated or Private deployments help with strict residency; hosted can be region-restricted in many cases if the model and hardware are available. we'll include region options in the doc.
[03:10] Priya Nair: logging who owns the audit logs and how long are they retained?
[03:16] Avery Chen: audit logs are available to the customer; for hosted we retain them 90 days by default, with add-on retention available. Dedicated/Private give you longer retention and direct access to logs in your cloud account.
[03:27] Diego Ramos: perfect. On the service account: we'll create a role with read-only S3 and pass the ARN. Do you need cross-account role or keys?
[03:35] Samir Patel: cross-account role for read-only S3 is best. avoids sharing long-lived keys. we'll provide the trust policy template.
[03:42] Maya Thompson: next: do you have any runbook for a failing node? we need to know how failover happens.
[03:47] Samir Patel: runtime is multi-node with autoscaling; if a node fails we have auto-restart and request routing to healthy nodes, plus fallback to a smaller-capacity variant if needed. for Dedicated we can set SLA and reserve burst capacity.
[04:02] Diego Ramos: fine. For the benchmark, when can we run it?
[04:05] Avery Chen: propose week of 2026-03-16. gives time to hand off creds and for Samir to prepare scripts.
[04:11] Maya Thompson: that works for our team.
[04:13] Priya Nair: we'll aim to provide access by 2026-03-09.
[04:17] Avery Chen: great. Quick check on model selection are you leaning open models or want Redwood-curated defaults?
[04:22] Maya Thompson: open models to start, we also want to evaluate Redwood's recommended quantized variant for cost.
[04:28] Samir Patel: we'll include two model profiles: a higher-accuracy float model and a quantized performance model; we'll run both in the benchmark.
[04:36] Diego Ramos: any prerequisites for the VPC peering? we usually need a maintenance window.
[04:40] Avery Chen: you'll need to open for the peering IPs and schedule a 30-minute window; we can do blue-green for the peering change if you prefer.
[04:47] Maya Thompson: ok. Can we get a one-pager on pricing and expected cost per 1M tokens for the two model profiles?
[04:53] Avery Chen: yes, I'll include a pricing sheet estimate and a worked example for the 1M token case.
[04:58] Priya Nair: last question do you support SAML SSO for the console?
[05:02] Avery Chen: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for user accounts in Dedicated/Private. hosted also supports SAML but some features vary.
[05:09] Maya Thompson: thanks.
[05:11] Samir Patel: i'll run through the benchmark plan after the call and attach sample prompts.
[05:16] Avery Chen: recap: we'll send security binder, network diagram, pricing sheet; customer to create cross-account role and share CIDR; schedule benchmark for 3/16 week. Anything else?
[05:27] Priya Nair: please include the retention numbers in writing.
[05:30] Avery Chen: will do.
[05:34] Maya Thompson: thanks all. good sync.
[05:36] Diego Ramos: thanks.
[05:37] Avery Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding progress, access and network setup, security requirements, and scheduling a benchmark run. Redwood will share SOC2 and security binder, network diagram, and pricing. Customer to provide cross-account S3 role and VPC CIDR; target benchmark week of 2026-03-16.
